tagline: Over the replanted Burn and down to the puffin rocks.
intro: The Coast Range starts to rise at Banks, among farms and vineyards, and OR 6 heads west into the Tillamook State Forest. Near the Gales Creek Overlook the first of the Tillamook Burn fires started in 1933, and the road twists along the Devils Lake Fork of the Wilson River through a forest put back with 72 million seedlings, with helicopters and hand planters both at the work. Idiotville, a salvage camp so remote that only an idiot would work there, has left nothing behind but the name of a creek.
Out of the mountains the land opens into dairy pasture at Tillamook, and OR 131 carries on west to Netarts Bay and north along the shore.

moments.title: Tillamook Forest Center
moments.text: A 40-foot replica fire lookout marks the entrance, and behind the center a suspension bridge crosses the Wilson River, where salmon can be spotted below.

moments.title: Oceanside
moments.text: From this beach two young men photographed Three Arch Rocks, half a mile offshore, and the hunters at work on them, until Theodore Roosevelt made the rocks a refuge in 1907.

moments.title: Cape Meares
moments.text: At the end of the road a short hike from the parking lot finds the Octopus Tree, a many-trunked Sitka spruce, near the lighthouse whose lens once flashed red and white by turns.
